subject: Bridgewell deployment: VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups
messages:
From: Sara Hansen <sara.hansen@bridgewell.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@bridgewell.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgewell deployment: VPC data flow & privacy follow-ups

Hi Irene / Ben —

Thanks for the call today — helpful to see the proposed topology. I'm attaching the network diagram the infra team pulled together (bridgewell_network_diagram_v1.pdf). A short list of follow-ups from our security and compliance checks:

1) PII handling: can Redwood guarantee that raw customer inputs (text, files) never leave our VPC in plaintext? Where do generated artifacts / KV cache entries live by default?
2) Data retention & logging: what controls exist to truncate or redact logs? What's the minimum retention window we can request for audit/logs and for request/response payloads?
3) Log access & segregation: who at Redwood can access raw logs and how are access events audited?
4) Egress & network boundaries: we prefer outbound egress to be limited to a small set of IPs or a PrivateLink endpoint. Can you provide egress IP ranges and an approach for static egress?
5) Air-gapped / on-prem option: we need a short checklist of what's required for an air-gapped pilot (physical handoff, images, key exchange).

Timeline: our pilot team wants to spin up an initial sandbox in early June if answers are in line with compliance.

Can you send a concise response to each bullet and a proposed next-step schedule? Also cc'ed Tom (platform security) — he may have follow-ups.

Thanks,

Sara Hansen
Head of Cloud Ops | Bridgewell Financial

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list and the diagram. High-level answers below; I'm attaching a short security snapshot that covers our Private/VPC posture. For deeper details, Marcus will follow up on the egress/firewall specifics.

Summary answers (short):
- PII: By default in a Redwood Private deployment, customer request payloads and model state (KV cache) are stored within the customer VPC or on-prem datastore and not persisted in our multi-tenant control plane. We can provide an option to disable KV cache persistence entirely for the pilot.
- Retention & logging: Audit and request logs are configurable per account. Minimum configurable retention for request/response artifacts is 7 days (short-term), and we support export to a customer S3/GCS bucket for longer retention/archival. Redaction: we offer field-level redaction rules but note that automated semantic redaction is best-effort — we recommend a final manual review for high-risk fields.
- Log access: Access is limited to named SRE/security accounts and all accesses are logged to the audit trail (immutable). We can provide an access list and examples of audit entries.
- Egress & static IPs: We offer two models — static egress IPs from a dedicated NAT pool, or private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Endpoint) into Redwood endpoints. Marcus will provide the exact CIDRs and ports.
- Air-gapped/on-prem: We support a packaged on-prem deployment. Requirements: isolated VM hosts (preferably with a local artifact store), offline installer images, and a KMS handshake (customer-provided HSM or our KMS connector). We'll send a one-page checklist for the pilot.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marcus to provide egress CIDRs + firewall matrix (by Mon EOD) — owner: Marcus Lin
- Provide a short doc with retention options and redaction configuration — owner: Irene (Wed)
- Schedule a security deep-dive with Bridgewell security (Tom + team) — propose Tue Jun 1 10:00 ET

I've attached our RDW private deploy snapshot for your review. If anything above doesn't align with your expectations, flag it and we'll adjust.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

Hi team — following on Irene's summary, below are the technical specifics we recommend for Bridgewell's pilot and a pre-flight checklist. I'll be available on Tue for the security deep-dive.

Egress and network boundaries (recommended):
- Preferred: AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Endpoint to Redwood ingress endpoints. This avoids public egress and is the lowest risk.
- Alternate: Dedicated NAT with static egress IPs from our dedicated NAT pool. We can publish up to 4 /32 addresses for firewall allowlisting.
- Minimal outbound ports: 443 (HTTPS) to configured endpoints; optional outbound 123 (NTP) if your hosts block it.

Sample internal address plan (for pilot topology):
- RDW inference nodes: 10.40.10.0/24
- KV cache/data plane: 10.40.11.0/24
- Management/monitoring: 10.40.12.0/26

Logging & retention:
- Audit logs: immutable audit trail for admin actions — we recommend exporting to your S3 with lifecycle policy. Retention options: 7d, 30d, 90d (configurable).
- Request/response artifacts: configurable min retention = 7 days; recommended for audit = 90 days, with export to your bucket.
- Access control: only named SRE and Security roles can access raw artifacts. All reads are recorded with timestamp, user, and reason.

PII controls & redaction:
- Field-level redaction rules can be applied at ingest (regex-based) and we offer a pre-processing hook to run customer-supplied redaction logic. We do NOT guarantee perfect semantic PII removal unless combined with a supervised eval.

Air-gapped / on-prem checklist (pilot):
- Host inventory and network diagram (received)
- Offline installer images (we provide) + checksum file
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM or approved key exchange procedure
- Local artifact store (NFS/S3-compatible) for model shards and logs
- Operator runbook + remote troubleshooting plan (if remote connectivity allowed)

Pre-flight items we need from Bridgewell:
1) Confirm PrivateLink vs NAT option and any existing VPC endpoints (owner: Tom)
2) Provide an S3 bucket ARN for log export and a retention policy you prefer (owner: Sara)
3) Confirm whether you want KV persistence disabled for the pilot (owner: Platform team)

I'll attach a short firewall matrix and the four static egress /32s in the follow-up email.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
